item.text: The physics bounds do not rule out the targets, but none of the precomputed cells clearly meets all three. The search is now exploring the family parameters for a candidate to certify.

The search found a BCC strut candidate with estimated relative density 17.54%, C44 of 3.40 GPa, and a complete gap covering 287–353 kHz. Certification is now checking those estimates; they are not yet sufficient to release the design.
Certification is still running. It checks stiffness across three mesh resolutions and verifies the complete gap over the Brillouin zone, with numerical error guards.
The certification tool has not returned a verdict yet. Release remains conditional on its results for density, C44, and the full requested gap.
Certification is still pending, with no intermediate results reported.
The solver is still working on the same candidate. I’m waiting for its verdict before deciding whether the design can be released.
While certification runs, one scope limit matters: the tools model 316L using its elastic constants and density. They do not verify LPBF feature sizes, supports, or powder removal.

item.text: Released a certified 5 mm 316L BCC cell with strut radius 0.319565 mm and node radius 1.272725 mm. Certified bounds give relative density ≤17.60%, C44 ≥3.013 GPa, and a complete gap covering 287–353 kHz. Certification applies to nominal geometry; erosion robustness failed, and LPBF manufacturability was not evaluated.
